text:
I agree that it definitely went downhill, but there's a design philosophy that remained at PES, making it still better in pure handling of the ball that FIFA never had. 

In FIFA if a player has 80/100 for a stat like shooting and you give the same input 80% of the time it will perform that action perfectly and 20% will fail.

In PES if a player has 80/100 it will widen or narrow the timing window you can pull off a good shot, so giving the perfect input will result in 100% perfect shots. It also means that a good player can play with shitty players and still try hard shots because a perfect input will produce a perfect strike. It doesn't get a random fail state applied to it. 

This results in the ball feeling far more independent, and a real feeling of satisfaction when scoring a outside of the box volley. While in FIFA still it's a game about playing the odds. You know that certain shots have a higher percentage chance than others, so you stop trying them when it matters.
